request: User asked to move build/research to the external T7 disk ("по диску можем наверное research перенести на внешний диск T7?"); internal data volume had 22 GiB free
preflight: no process had files open under build/research (lsof)
only build/research/e2e changed after 2026-10-01 (app_e2e captures); it was excluded and stays in place
other worktrees live on X5; 137 symlinks (134 to /Volumes/X5/ntsd-2.4-research), no hardlinks
format: PAX tar via bsdtar --format pax --no-mac-metadata --no-xattrs --no-acls --no-fflags; entries >=64 MiB get their own archive, smaller ones are batched in ~2 GiB
verification: each archive streamed to T7 with F_NOCACHE then F_FULLFSYNC while its SHA-256 was computed
per-member readback from T7 (F_NOCACHE): name, type, mode, nanosecond mtime from the PAX header, symlink target, SHA-256 body against the source; no extra or missing members
whole-file SHA-256 re-read from the device equal to the streamed digest
the source entry was removed only after these checks passed
final pass after all writes: 159 archives, 132,219,115,520 bytes re-read with F_NOCACHE in 350 s, 0 mismatches
trial: the first archive (active-gameplay-attempt2) was written before F_NOCACHE was added; its device SHA-256 matched immediately and again in the final pass
restore: tar -xpf <archive> -C build/research (bsdtar restores modes, links and nanosecond mtimes from the PAX headers); the index maps each top-level entry to its archive
notes: macOS created AppleDouble ._*.tar files next to archives on ExFAT for their extended attributes; they are not part of the archives
about 700 repository files (mostly historical docs and frozen tools) name build/research paths; those inputs must now be restored from T7 before reuse

66 small files under build/research were tracked by git; the move showed them as deleted. They were restored from HEAD (git checkout -- build/research) the same evening. They exist in git and in the archives, and tools/archive_to_t7.py now skips entries with tracked files unless --include-tracked is given.
